clue.text: Mere game

definitions.meaning: a mere is a small lake or pond, a still body of water
a cue sport played on a table with pockets, like billiards or snooker

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses something as nothing more than a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mere' reads as the adjective 'only', but here it is the noun for a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mere is a small lake; separately, the word names the cue game played on a pocketed table.

clue.text: Matter about wise man looking up constellation

indicators.note: the word for matter goes around the reversed wise man

parts.note: pus is matter discharged from a wound

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up reads the wise man upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: Some matter concerning an astrologer gazing up at the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'looking up' means reading upwards, so backwards; 'about' wraps the matter around that.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large northern star group named after the winged horse of Greek myth.

clue.text: Monaco uncovered separate charge as an instalment

indicators.note: uncovered strips the first and last letters off the word Monaco

parts.note: in law, a count is one separate charge in an indictment

explanation.surface: Monaco is revealed to have levied a separate charge in part payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' takes ONAC from Monaco.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: paying something this way means paying part of it as an interim instalment towards the total owed.

clue.text: After year in London college, monk is messing up old genetic theory

indicators.note: the scrambled monk-is letters come after the college-with-year piece
the letter for year is placed inside the abbreviation for the college

parts.note: LSE is the London School of Economics

indicators.note: messing up the letters of monk is puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A monk, after a year at a London college, is muddling an outdated theory of heredity.
explanation.walkthrough: The London School of Economics is the college; 'messing up' scrambles MONK IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the discredited Soviet doctrine of Trofim Lysenko held that acquired traits are inherited, an obsolete genetics theory.

clue.text: Yeah, we organised shout at rodeos

indicators.note: organised means the letters of yeah we are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that they arranged a rodeo yell.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a whoop of exuberance associated with cowboys, typically heard at rodeos.

clue.text: Perhaps US door guard has missed second approach

indicators.note: the guard has missed out the letter for second

parts.note: a sentry is a soldier posted on guard
a way is a route or approach

explanation.surface: An American door guard misses a second approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has missed' removes S from SENTRY to give ENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an American word for an entrance passage, of which a door is one instance, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Put own employee under house arrest to retain capability

definitions.text: Put own employee under house arrest
definitions.meaning: read literally, to confine your own worker indoors
to keep up a skill through occasional practice

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a cryptic literal reading: one's own hand (worker) kept in (confined).
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase means to practise occasionally so as not to lose a skill.

clue.text: Vision of latter half of hadj?

indicators.note: only the second five letters of the ten-letter word for the hadj are kept

parts.note: the hadj is the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca

explanation.surface: A sight seen at the end of a journey to Mecca.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the hadj is replaced by a synonym before half is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mental picture or something seen in the mind's eye.

clue.text: Much of significance about lake pigment

indicators.note: the shortened significance word goes around the letter for lake
most of the significance word is used, dropping its last letter

parts.note: meaning is significance
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A pigment found by a lake proves highly significant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much of' cuts MEANING to MEANIN, which 'about' puts around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the dark brown substance that colours human skin, hair and eyes.

clue.text: Certainly, yours truly is not concerned about current dog

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker, I
don't mind means not to care about something
I is the symbol for electric current
Fido is a stock name for a dog

annotation.spelling: I DON'T MIND IF I DO

explanation.surface: The speaker shrugs off worries about a dog that is in the room at present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' is the physics symbol I, not 'present day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a hearty phrase of acceptance used when offered something, much like saying yes, gladly.

clue.text: Noble reduced allowance astrologer is after

indicators.note: the astrologer's name follows the shortened allowance
the allowance word is cut short by losing its final letter

parts.note: a grant is a sum allowed or given, such as a student allowance
John Dee was the Elizabethan astrologer and magician

explanation.surface: A nobleman pursued by an astrologer, his allowance cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' trims GRANT to GRAN; John Dee was Elizabeth I's court astrologer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a Spanish or Portuguese nobleman of the highest rank, hence any person of high standing.

clue.text: Girl in work in a chiropodist's concern

indicators.note: the girl's name goes inside the word for work

parts.note: toil is hard work
Ena is a girl's name, common in crosswords

explanation.surface: A girl at work, perhaps employed in a foot clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does two jobs in the surface: the first one signals the insertion, the second is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: chiropodists treat feet, and an ingrowing nail on a toe is a classic problem they deal with.

clue.text: Odds-on mercenary destroyed school in the past

indicators.note: destroyed signals the letters of odds-on mercenary are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A favoured hired soldier wrecked a school some time ago.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain these were state schools, from 1944 to the 1970s, for pupils who did not pass the eleven-plus exam into grammar school.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a former type of British state secondary school, now largely replaced by comprehensives, so a school of the past.

clue.text: Like bad housing, oh dear, after much economic downturn

indicators.note: the exclamation comes after the shortened downturn word
much of the downturn word means all but its last letter is used

parts.note: a slump is a sharp fall in economic activity
'my!' is an exclamation of dismay like oh dear

explanation.surface: Bad housing follows a long economic downturn, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'much' means most of the word, here all but its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: squalid and run-down, characteristic of a slum, an area of poor, overcrowded dwellings.

clue.text: Prone to try for concessions in confrontation

definitions.meaning: lying flat with the front of the body downwards

definitions.text: to try for concessions in confrontation
definitions.meaning: to confront someone boldly until they back off or give way

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: lying prone means lying front downwards, and the phrasal verb means to defeat opposition by confronting it head-on.

clue.text: Clothier's forbidden more trim

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: out as in ruled out, not allowed
fitter means in better shape, trimmer

explanation.surface: A tailor is banned from slimming down further.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a seller of clothes and equipment, especially for a particular activity, like a clothes merchant.

clue.text: Bird dropping fine maggot and caterpillar

indicators.note: the bird is dropping the letter for fine

parts.note: a finch is a small seed-eating bird
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
a maggot is a grub or worm

explanation.surface: A bird's dropping lands on a fine maggot and a caterpillar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' looks like bird mess but removes F from FINCH to leave INCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the looper larva of a geometrid moth, a caterpillar that moves by arching its body.

clue.text: How stamps can be posted — about five pairs with article

indicators.note: the word for posted wraps around the number and the article

parts.note: sent, as a letter is posted
five pairs make ten
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Instructions on mailing stamps, covering five pairs and an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How stamps can be posted' looks like one definition, but 'posted' belongs to the wordplay; 'about' signals the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Philatelic term: stamps printed joined together in a sheet but differing in design or value are described with this French phrase.

clue.text: Covers students' union over black mark

indicators.note: in a down clue, over turns the combined pieces upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: tops are covers or lids
NUS is the National Union of Students in Britain

explanation.surface: A student union covers up a blot on its record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses TOPS+NUS. The NUS is the UK's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a dark patch appearing on the surface of the sun, literally a black mark there.

clue.text: Injunction about little house in high country

indicators.note: the word for injunction goes around the small dwelling

parts.note: a ban is a prohibiting order
a hut is a small, simple house

explanation.surface: A court order concerning a small cottage up in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high country' is a fair definition: this Himalayan kingdom is among the most mountainous nations; 'about' signals the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Himalayan kingdom, mountainous and lying at great altitude between India and Tibet.

clue.text: Uncared-for state's new elite around top of government

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the elite word goes around the government's first letter

parts.note: the elect are a chosen elite

indicators.note: top of the word government, in a down clue, is its first letter

explanation.surface: A new elite surrounds the head of a government that has been left untended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts G inside ELECT, after N.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the condition of being left without proper care or attention.

clue.text: Horse eating tip of yew was in agony

indicators.note: the horse takes in the letter as if eating it

parts.note: a steed is a horse

indicators.note: here tip means the final letter, the bottom end of the word yew

explanation.surface: A horse that ate yew leaves suffered terribly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip of' gives W, the end of yew, not Y; 'eating' puts it inside STEED. Yew is poisonous to horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to stew is to fret or suffer in a state of anxiety, so being in torment.

clue.text: Although anything but a fool, a good person in passing

parts.note: as in 'he is no fool', no means anything but
a twit is a foolish person

indicators.note: the saint abbreviation goes inside the word for passing

parts.note: handing is passing something over
ST, short for saint, is a good person

explanation.surface: Someone is far from foolish, yet a saint in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anything but a fool' reads as 'no fool'; 'in' signals the saint going inside the passing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both are conjunctions meaning in spite of the fact that, introducing a concession.

clue.text: What's taking place in First Empire times

indicators.note: what is taking place in the words is the run of letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A question about events in Napoleon's First Empire period.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across firsT EMPIre.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a musical term: speeds or time measures in music, the Italian plural of tempo.

clue.text: I am in place, I note, round London district

indicators.note: the contraction of I am sits inside the abbreviation for place

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
I'm is the contraction of I am
C is a musical note
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone says they are in position, noting a round of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the contraction sitting inside the street-name abbreviation; 'round' is the shape O.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an area of central London in Westminster, south of Victoria station, known for its stucco terraces.

clue.text: Engine inventor is to cut deal?

definitions.meaning: Sir Frank, the British engineer who invented the turbojet engine
to pare wood with a knife; deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' looks like a bargain but is softwood timber; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Name and verb: the jet engine pioneer shared his surname with the word for carving wood by shaving off slivers.

clue.text: Fashioned model tiara, created to fit

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or formed, so the letters of model tiara are reshaped

explanation.surface: A tiara for a model was made to measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something made specially for a particular person or purpose, as a suit cut to the wearer's measurements.

clue.text: Get irritated with mist coming off the sea

definitions.meaning: a sea fog that rolls in on the coast, especially in eastern England

explanation.walkthrough: The sea mist sense is chiefly a regional word on the east coast of Britain, often as 'sea fret'.
explanation.definitionFit: Double sense: the verb means to worry and be agitated; the noun is a coastal fog drifting inland.
